text:
sam: Quick FYI - were kicking off a tiny canary for the route-broker negotiation header `X-RI-Route-Broker`. Need minimal SDK support so clients can opt in and we can measure adoption.

nina: Important question - do we force users to provide JSON objects? lots of code just sets Route-Hint to a string. SDK should be flexible.

diego: Agreed. SDK contract suggestion: new param `route_broker` accepts object | string. If string, SDK will wrap: {"route": <string>}. Also send legacy `Route-Hint` alongside while canary is active.

nina: Implementation detail: expose opt-in flag `enable_route_broker: bool` default false. Also respect env var `REDWOOD_ENABLE_ROUTE_BROKER=true` for internal test apps.

sam: Telemetry needs: emit `sdk.route_broker.handshake` with keys: `sdk_name`, `sdk_version`, `opted_in`. Console wants to map this to an adoption metric.

ux-bot: Console/telemetry: we'll add two small tiles - "Broker adoption" (percent of requests with handshake) and "Quota deltas" (compare enforcement rate pre/post). Well need `client_id` in the broker payload to stitch traces.

diego: We can add `client_id` and `sdk_name`. Make `client_id` generated per-install and stable; no user data.

nina: Tests: add unit tests for header serialization + a little e2e against `GET /v1/route-broker/debug` that echoes parsed header. QA should run against internal org.

qa: we can run nightly canary job and exercise sample workloads. What are rollback thresholds?

deploy-bot: deploy scheduled: route-broker v0.1-canary -> infra-canary. Rollback if 5xx rate increases > 1.5x OR tenant quota mismatch > 3% within first 15m.

sam: Semver plan: ship minimal SDK updates (no breaking API): py 1.8.1, go v0.12.1, ts 2.3.1. These add the flag + helper that accepts str|obj. Add example snippets in migration doc.

nina: Example snippets (add to docs):

```python
# python
client = RedwoodClient(enable_route_broker=True)
client.generate(prompt, route_broker={"route":"/dedicated/pool-2","client_id":"cli_abc"})
```

```ts
// typescript
const client = new Redwood({ enableRouteBroker: true });
client.generate(prompt, { routeBroker: { route: '/dedicated/pool-2', clientId: 'cli_abc' } });
```

```go
// go
c := redwood.NewClient(redwood.WithEnableRouteBroker(true))
c.Generate(ctx, prompt, redwood.RouteBroker{"route":"/dedicated/pool-2","client_id":"cli_abc"})
```

nina: Also, SDKs should gracefully accept user-provided non-JSON: if header passed as raw string parse to {"route": <string>} and emit a warning telemetry `sdk.route_broker.warn_parse`.

diego: Server-side: add a short-lived feature flag `force_broker_for_internal` so we can flip broker header for internal test apps without SDK change. Helpful for QA.

sam: Action items: nina -> open SDK PRs (py/ts/go) w/ tests + changelog. diego -> server flag and debug endpoint. ux-bot -> telemetry mappings + dashboard tile. qa -> run canary runbook. deploy-bot -> deploy tomorrow 03:30 UTC.

nina: I'll include migration checklist in changelog and a one-pager for support.

diego: ack. Ill add server-side runbook notes for rollback triggers.

qa: ack - will prepare tests and run list.

sam: thanks, everyone. Keep messages short in PRs so we can review fast. :thumbsup: (end)
